clue.text: Marry but don't be having children, the pestilential creatures

parts.note: s.p., short for Latin sine prole, means without issue, the genealogists' note for dying childless
lice are verminous pests that spread disease

explanation.surface: A grim warning: wed if you must, but keep clear of breeding the little horrors.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole, 'without offspring') is a convention from family trees; the 'children' look like part of the marriage advice but are an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is informal slang for joining a couple in wedlock, as in getting spliced.

clue.text: Ursa, non-U version, entertaining cupbearer

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece goes around the other
a version is a rendering in a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
non-U literally says without U, so that letter comes out of the word

parts.note: Hebe was the cupbearer to the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A posh-or-common usage note about the Great Bear, oddly hosting a mythological waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is British slang for lower-class usage, a red herring here; it simply means 'without U', and 'version' then rearranges what is left (SAR) around the cupbearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa is the Latin word for a female bear, as in the constellations Ursa Major and Minor.

clue.text: Light in a pencil, as erasable?

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a mark made in pencil can be rubbed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser is a device emitting an intense beam, so it serves as a kind of light.

clue.text: Grant formerly given in successive notes

indicators.note: given in says the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: C, D and E follow one another in the musical scale
once means at a former time

explanation.surface: A grant that used to be awarded in a series of instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes are consecutive letters of the musical scale; the word for 'formerly' is slipped in after the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point in argument is to admit or yield it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: He's accustomed to bark

parts.note: reads like a dog used to barking, but bark is also barque, a sailing ship, so this is an old sailor at home on one

explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned old sailor is well used to life aboard a barque.

clue.text: A murder detected by sensitive listener

indicators.note: a detected crime is one worked out and reconstructed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A killing uncovered thanks to someone with keen hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detected' is the anagram signal, rearranging A MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the delicate membrane that picks up sound vibrations, so it is a sensitive listening organ.

clue.text: Depression is the attempt to revert to the oral stage?

definitions.text: to revert to the oral stage?

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A psychoanalytic quip: depression as a bid to regress to Freud's oral phase.
explanation.walkthrough: The Freudian 'oral stage' is a red herring; the definition jokes that dentistry is work done on the mouth, a stage for oral matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentistry is the treatment of teeth, the whimsical oral stage that patients return to.

clue.text: It's sweet to stick around 19

indicators.note: around tells us the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to glue is to stick things together
19 is the salad green clue, and cos is a variety of that leaf

explanation.surface: Something sugary that clings to a reference elsewhere in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' refers to the answer of clue 19, a salad leaf; a variety of it, not the answer itself, is what goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar, so it is a sweet substance.

clue.text: Dated tile?

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat, so an elderly piece of headgear also stands for anything out of date

explanation.definitionFit: Something hackneyed or out of fashion is called this, and literally it is an aged bowler.

clue.text: It is not what he is that makes our planner snoop

definitions.text: It is not what he is

indicators.note: makes says the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a planner's prying amounts to, and what it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' is grammatically this class of word, and the joke is that 'it', though technically one too, hardly sounds personal. 'makes' rearranges OUR PLANNER SNOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: He belongs to the grammatical class of words standing for a speaker, listener or third party.

clue.text: 2 of 3 in boat taking on 1 of fab 4

indicators.note: taking means adding the following word on at the end

parts.note: George is one of the trio in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
Harris is another of the three men in Jerome's boat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two of a famous boating trio take aboard one of a famous pop foursome.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat (1889) features J, George and Harris; the Fab Four are the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Beatles' lead guitarist, one of the band nicknamed the Fab Four.

clue.text: See 10
Look with mine in view?

parts.note: searching the ground for ore in hope of opening a mine; the word also means a view

explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to search land for minerals, and as a noun it also means a vista.

clue.text: Broadcaster holding barrier to swordsman, as it were

indicators.note: holding means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a sower broadcasts, scattering seed by hand
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: A radio presenter keeping a fencer at bay behind a barricade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' suggests radio, but it is someone who scatters seed. A sword-swallower is the 'swordsman, as it were'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-swallower downs blades, so this swallower is jokingly a kind of swordsman.

clue.text: Not fancy one that tangles with a cancelled performance

parts.note: something that mats hair or fibres is jokingly a matter
a cancelled event is off
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Someone plain in taste caught up in a show that was called off.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER is an invented 'one who mats', not the everyday word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain, prosaic manner without frills is unfancy, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: See 14
Dad tailed and topped goose

indicators.note: tailed means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: dad means father

indicators.note: topped means its first letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A father docked and beheaded like a bird for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad' is used twice: FATHER without its tail gives FATHE, and DAD without its top gives AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose is an old word for a silly person, and so is a dimwit called this.

clue.text: American writer for the Thunderer said O!

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: said tells us the following word is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: the exclamation O

explanation.surface: An exclamation uttered on behalf of a thundering god, or a famous newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is also a nickname for The Times newspaper, a misleading path. EAU, French for water, is pronounced like O.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, author of Walden, was a nineteenth-century US essayist.

clue.text: Start game with tyrant on holiday

parts.note: a bully is a tyrant
off work means on holiday

explanation.surface: Kicking off a match with a despot who is away on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: A bully-off starts a game of field hockey, with two players tapping sticks before striking the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In field hockey, play formerly began with this face-off between two opponents.

clue.text: Farewell to extras

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bye is an extra run scored without the bat, so two of them

explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual parting phrase, and also literally two cricket byes, runs counted as extras.

clue.text: Some salad, shall we say?

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, so we want what it sounds like

parts.note: shall we means let us

explanation.surface: Proposing to serve some greens, as one might suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy vegetable forms the base of most green salads.

clue.text: Puzzle: cor! Nearly eaten by earth-dweller

indicators.note: eaten by means the first piece goes inside the creature's mouth, enclosed

parts.note: a fox lives in an earth, its den

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: cor and lummy are both British exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry of surprise from someone almost swallowed by an underground creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter of the exclamation, leaving LUMM; a fox's den is called an earth, hence 'earth-dweller'.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle someone completely is to puzzle them, a direct synonym verb.

clue.text: Saint (it doesn't 14 in the least) Sylvester

parts.note: with 14 as matter, it doesn't matter in the least is it's all one

explanation.surface: A saint named Sylvester, of no consequence at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is MATTER(-of-fact); 'it's all one' is an idiom meaning it makes no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester is the first name of the actor who played Rocky and Rambo.

clue.text: Say what you may say is a decorative force

indicators.note: say asks for what the following word sounds like when spoken

parts.note: talk is what you may say, as in spoken words

explanation.surface: Speak your mind: there is an ornamental power at work.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech TALK and the answer sound alike. The answer is both a twisting force and, as a variant of torc, an ancient ornamental neck ring.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rotational force in physics and also an ornamental Celtic neck-ring.

clue.text: Children always like a bit of kidney

indicators.note: a bit means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Youngsters are always fond of eating a morsel of kidney.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to the kidneys, as in medical terms for those organs.

clue.text: Dividing 9s — don't tell anyone!

parts.note: between means dividing, separating two things
9 is a personal pronoun, and you and me are two of those

explanation.surface: A confidential aside about splitting something up.
explanation.walkthrough: '9s' refers to the 9-across answer type: YOU AND ME are two such words, and BETWEEN them is literally dividing them.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase introduces a secret, asking the hearer to keep it confidential.

clue.text: King of Persia bringing about raid on America

indicators.note: about signals turning the letters around into a new order

parts.note: US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A Persian monarch launching an attack on the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RAID to give DARI, followed by US.
explanation.definitionFit: Darius the Great was an Achaemenid ruler of the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Automatic response to law enforcer's law

parts.note: a referee enforces the laws of a game, ref for short
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A knee-jerk reaction to a police officer's ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an involuntary reaction, a synonym for an automatic response.
